grace-baptist-cape-coral-ascol-fl.assessment: Grace Baptist Church Cape Coral, founded 1983, has been pastored by Dr. Tom Ascol since 1986 — nearly 40 years of confessional Reformed Baptist preaching. grace-church-lynchburg-efca.assessment: Grace Church Lynchburg is an Evangelical Free Church of America congregation with 35+ years of faithful ministry in the Lynchburg/Madison Heights corridor. Founded in 1988, Grace Church has served through six rented facilities and is now building a permanent home across from its current meeting place at Monelison Middle School — a sign of a congregation committed to long-term community investment. The EFCA is one of the strongest evangelical networks for theological accountability: clear confessional statement on inerrancy, male-only senior pastors, Great Commission mission, and strong doctrinal formation. For a man in the Madison Heights/Lynchburg area wanting a smaller, community-embedded church with solid evangelical credentials, Grace Church EFCA is worth visiting.

grace-community-church-chesapeake.assessment: Grace Community Church in Chesapeake is a small-to-medium non-denominational congregation led by Pastor Stephen Hildebrandt. The church distinguishes itself in Hampton Roads by its commitment to expository teaching — chapter by chapter, verse by verse, precept upon precept. This is one of the strongest indicators of a healthy teaching church. The home fellowship model (Sunday afternoon gatherings in homes throughout Chesapeake) reflects a shepherding culture that goes beyond Sunday-only programming. Hildebrandt's personal testimony — an aerospace engineer who came to Christ and found his calling in ministry — suggests depth and earnest faith. Key unknowns: formal statement of faith, elder gender policy, and church accountability structure. For men in Chesapeake who want a teaching church with real community, GCC deserves serious investigation. The expository approach and home fellowship culture set it apart from most Hampton Roads options.

grace-episcopal-grand-rapids-mi.assessment: Grace Episcopal Church is the historic home parish of President Gerald R. Ford and Betty Ford, who were married in the old sanctuary in 1948 and whose private funeral was held here in 2006. The parish remains beautiful and historic, with strong choral and liturgical traditions in the Episcopal style. However, for the MOOP rubric, Grace is firmly within The Episcopal Church (TEC) — a denomination that since 1976 has ordained women to all orders, since 2003 has consecrated openly gay bishops, and since 2015 has authorized same-sex marriage rites. These denominational positions place Grace at red on cultural, gender, and denominational dimensions of the rubric. The parish is in a season of transition following the 2024 dissolution-by-merger of the Episcopal Diocese of Western Michigan into the new Diocese of the Great Lakes. Beautiful history. Significant theological distance from MOOP's confessional commitments.

grace-fellowship-efca-fredericksburg.assessment: Grace Fellowship Church is an EFCA congregation in the historic College Heights area near UMW. The EFCA is a solidly evangelical denomination — inerrantist, complementarian, missions-focused, and known for expository preaching. Grace Fellowship explicitly practices elder-led congregationalism and expository preaching. Sunday School is offered for all ages, Children's Church is provided, and a weekly Bible study runs mid-week. The informal but organized worship style (mix of hymns and contemporary praise) suits a broad range of evangelical preferences. Located near the university, this church likely draws a thoughtful, theologically engaged congregation. A serious option for a man who wants EFCA doctrinal clarity and accountability.

grace-memorial-baptist-bedford.assessment: Grace Memorial Baptist Church in Bedford is a rural SBC congregation with exactly the kind of pastoral stability that builds genuine community: Pastor Greg Rogers has served since 2000 — over 25 years of faithful shepherd ministry in the same Bedford County community. The church's motto ('A Friendly Place to Grow in Grace') reflects a congregation known for genuine warmth and welcome. SBC of Virginia affiliation provides Baptist Faith & Message 2000 accountability on Scripture, gender, and soteriology. For a man looking for a smaller, community-rooted SBC church outside of Lynchburg proper, with a long-tenured pastor and genuine Bedford County connections, Grace Memorial Baptist is an excellent option.

Pastor Russ Whitfield sits on the Alliance for Mission and Renewal (AMR) Executive Board — the soft-progressive PCA advocacy group in the Keller / Redeemer-network mold (a4mr.org). Whitfield also signed the December 2025 PCA "Call to Prayer & Lament" (pcaprayerandlament.com) — a left-leaning open letter spearheaded by Irwyn Ince and Duke Kwon lamenting "schismatic culture," sidelining of women, doctrinal "rigidity," and racial microaggressions in the PCA. Joel Littlepage also concluded his Associate Pastor role August 2025. The KH first-hand testimony (female shepherdesses, CRT, racially segregated events) STILL STANDS regardless of pastor turnover — it reflects church culture, not just one pastor — so the BLACK rating is preserved. But future research should re-cross-check the new lead pastor against the 7 statement lists.

grace-presbyterian-pca-aiken-sc.assessment: Grace Presbyterian Church is a confessional Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) congregation in Aiken, South Carolina, holding the Westminster Confession and Catechisms as “our only rule for faith and life.” It keeps the traditional Reformed rhythm — morning and evening worship, Wednesday men’s and women’s Bible studies, and a monthly Lord’s Supper — and is led by a plurality of male elders under Palmetto Presbytery. An acquaintance of MOOP whose family attends describes the pastor as excellent and the culture as explicitly patriarchal and family-integrated, with head coverings common among the women and a large contingent of young families; the fellowship meals are a highlight and the main critique is simply a lengthy service. It earns green across all ten categories. (Identification note: an acquaintance of MOOP recommended “Grace Presbyterian (PCA)” without a city; this Aiken congregation is the strong match by denomination and proximity to the Springfield, SC daughter-church plant they described — confirm if a direct link is available.)

grace-reformed-church-dc.assessment: Grace Reformed Church is a historic Washington DC congregation with a fascinating history — it was the church of President Theodore Roosevelt during his time in the White House. Originally an Evangelical and Reformed Church congregation, it merged into the United Church of Christ (UCC) in 1957. Today the UCC is one of the most theologically liberal denominations in America, fully affirming LGBTQ+ clergy and same-sex marriage, rejecting biblical inerrancy, and embracing pluralistic soteriology. Individual UCC congregations vary in their degree of liberalism, but the denomination provides no orthodox accountability. The historic building and Roosevelt connection make it interesting from a historical standpoint, but for a man seeking biblically sound Word ministry and gospel-centered community, Grace Reformed DC is not recommended. Seek out Reformed churches in the area that have maintained confessional integrity.

gracelife-church-spruce-grove-ab-canada.assessment: GraceLife Church Spruce Grove (Edmonton metro AB Canada) under Pastor James Coates is internationally known for a 2021 civil-disobedience stand against Alberta COVID-19 public-health restrictions. Coates was arrested February 2021, held in custody after refusing bail conditions, released March 22 2021 after pleading guilty + paying $1,500 fine; charges later DROPPED September 2023 after the Ingram court ruling found Alberta's public-health orders had been improperly imposed under the Public Health Act. The stand made GraceLife a touchstone for biblical-conviction-vs-state-overreach within North American conservative Christianity. Reformed Baptist; expository preaching; male eldership.

grantham-church-mechanicsburg-pa.assessment: Grantham Church is the historic flagship of the Brethren in Christ U.S. denomination, founded near the campus of what is now Messiah University in Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania. Pastor David Flowers brings a serious academic-pastoral pedigree — biblical studies graduate degrees, 25+ years across Texas, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, and a published trajectory in New Testament studies and early Christian ethics. The Brethren in Christ tradition holds together Anabaptist peace witness with Wesleyan-Holiness soteriology and pietist devotion — a hybrid that produces mission-minded, Bible-loving congregations but with synergistic rather than Reformed soteriology. For a Mechanicsburg-area man wanting a Christ-centered, mission-oriented church with a graduate-degreed expositor in the pulpit, Grantham deserves a careful look. The denominational yellow flag is gender — BIC USA does permit women's ordination at congregational discretion, though Grantham's senior pastoral office is male.

score_notes.scripture: BIC affirms Scripture as inspired, authoritative Word of God; pastor holds biblical-studies graduate degree from evangelical seminary.

greater-tabernacle-mbc-sbc-lawrenceburg-.assessment: Greater Tabernacle Missionary Baptist (Lawrenceburg TN) called Rev. Shonda Reynolds Christian as senior pastor in June 2015 and was disfellowshipped by the Lawrence County Association of Baptists by a 73-4 vote on October 12, 2015 — the association explicitly citing the Baptist Faith and Message 2000 Article VI ('the office of pastor is limited to men as qualified by Scripture'). Pastor Christian, who continues to lead the church a decade later, publicly characterized the disfellowship as 'unchristian' and challenged the binding force of the 2000 BF&M revision.
